q: How should an Ankleshwar bulk drug unit count emissions from solvent recovery and incineration?
title: Ankleshwar API unit: solvent emissions
short: Steam and power used to distil solvents back for reuse are ordinary Scope 1 and 2. Solvent you burn in your own incinerator or thermal oxidiser is Scope 1 at its carbon content. Solvent waste sent to a common incinerator is Scope 3, Category 5, using the operator's figure or a stated estimate.
audience: Bulk drug and intermediate makers in Ankleshwar, Panoli and Jhagadia

ul: Recovered in house: count the steam and electricity used by the recovery columns.
Burnt in your own incinerator: Scope 1, carbon in the solvent converted to CO2, plus any support fuel.
Sent out to a common hazardous waste incinerator: Scope 3, waste generated in operations.

p: For a known solvent, the carbon fraction comes from its formula; toluene is about 91 percent carbon by mass, methanol about 37 percent. Multiply tonnes burnt by carbon fraction and by 44/12.
Solvent purchase invoices, recovery logs, incinerator feed records and manifests for waste sent out. They also support the solvent balance a pharma buyer may ask for.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, steam, electricity and raw material invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per unit, so a product figure can be traced back to the documents behind it.

sources.label: IPCC 2006 Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories
GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Standard

example.title: Worked example: 10 tonnes of toluene burnt in your own oxidiser
lines: Plus the support fuel burnt, from the fuel invoices
example.note: Carbon fractions come from the chemical formula. Mixed solvent streams need the mix from the recovery log.
